result.summary: Switches native Windows builds and CI from MSVC (cl.exe) to clang-cl, dropping support for compiling with cl.exe. CMake configuration, presets, compiler diagnostic flags, and feature introspection tests are adjusted to accommodate Clang's MSVC driver mode and link against the Clang runtime builtins library. Workarounds for MSVC compiler bugs and limitations, such as lack of constexpr byteswap and requires-expression bugs, are eliminated.
result.problem: MSVC (cl.exe) produces slower binaries, suffers from slower build times, lacks inline assembly support on x64 and ARM64 architectures, and frequently requires dedicated workarounds for internal compiler errors and language conformance bugs (#31456, #36153).
evidence: Author microbenchmarks show substantial validation performance improvements with clang-cl over MSVC on Windows, such as ConnectBlockAllEcdsa improving from 7.40 to 11.52 block/s (~55%) and DeserializeBlockTest improving from 121.46 to 189.04 block/s.
Author CI timing measurements show native Windows CI build time dropping from 20m 35s to 12m 43s (approx. 38% faster).
Resolves compiler bug workarounds documented in issues #31456, #14118, and #36153.

enables: Inline assembly optimizations on Windows (e.g., secp256k1 #1681)

result.scope_notes: Drops support for building with cl.exe entirely rather than supporting both cl.exe and clang-cl in parallel.
result.changed_since_previous: Removed prior dependency on #36554, and updated CMake checks across crypto, CRC32C, atomic, and sanitizer detection routines to compile warning-free under warnings-as-errors mode.
result.card: This pull request migrates native Windows builds and CI from MSVC (cl.exe) to clang-cl, dropping support for compiling with cl.exe. Switching to clang-cl eliminates maintenance overhead from MSVC compiler bugs (#31456, #36153) and unblocks inline assembly optimizations on Windows. Author benchmarks show block connection performance improving by over 50% alongside a 38% reduction in Windows CI build times. Native Windows developers must install the clang-cl toolset in Visual Studio or LLVM.

risk.why: A mistake could break native Windows compilation and Windows CI workflows, though official release binaries are cross-compiled using MinGW.
